review.summary: Phase 21's plan-and-provenance chunk delivers verifiable, well-scoped planning evidence and all five attempt-03 findings are genuinely closed with new regressions. I independently confirmed the provenance chain by reading bytes rather than prose: tools/red_team_management.py:35 pins the four audit inputs by SHA256; build() (401-467) checks the vendored contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml against the pinned inventory hash, requires openapi.json to parse equal to the YAML, and verify_management_metadata() (369-386) now asserts every source.json field (id/family/repository/commit/upstreamPath/sourceUrl/license/redistributed/usedForGeneration/path/sha256/bytes/gitBlobSha1/openapiVersion/apiVersion/expectedOperations/licensePath/licenseSha256/licenseSpdx/yamlParser) against the manifest entry, the actual spec and the license bytes, with a per-field damage test at tools/test_red_team_management.py:164-173. contracts/manifest.json:1949-1963 and 2442-2482 register the source plus four vendorArtifacts, and contracts/licenses/pan-dev-582e30543bf2.LICENSE (MIT, 283becab…) matches source.json:24. tools/verify-contracts.py:29/393-407/468-489 owns only the red-team-management product subtree, rejects unregistered version directories and requires exact corpus/manifest file-set equality, and its --self-test records 27 rejected tampering cases including nine new vendor-ownership cases. The 7-source/160-operation inventory reproduces (COUNTS 18+23+47+42+5+21+4=160), every operation carries native bindings, parameters, body, responses, security, servers and a full local-reference closure, and resolve_active_identity() (389-398) closes the identity loop for both manifest_source and source_metadata kinds. All 68 deltas are classified; I checked the substantive ones against vendor bytes (TargetConnectionType +VERTEX_AI/+N8N, ResponseMode +REALTIME, ProfilingStatus INIT/QUEUED→NOT_STARTED, ProfilingStatusFilter exactly four values, TargetStatusFilter narrowed 7→2) and every row of the plan's migration table at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:152-159 is accurate. The retention floor is loaded only from the hash-pinned immutable seed, uses an additive-only subset check, emits the current inventory with floorReference rather than a floor copy, and --verify-retention-origin rehashes all six ledgers. All 25 recorded checks are real invocations with exit_code 0, bound to source ae5352b1…, and match tools/check_phase.py management_commands(21) exactly. Remaining defects are robustness and editorial, not correctness: disposition() still fails open on renamed-component successors and on whole-subtree additions/prefix-matched component names, and the plan document carries pervasive typographic defects. No blocker or high findings.

findings.description: The 'removed' branch disposes renamed components on successor *existence* alone: for len(path)==3 removals it returns component_removed_or_renamed and build() (472-476) only asserts the successor name is present in the new schema set. No reviewed digest binds the successor's content and nothing compares the removed variant's members against it. This is not theoretical for the current diff. NativeConnectionParamsBase-Input/-Output were removed and merged into NativeConnectionParamsBase, and the merged successor adds MultiTurnClientSessionConfig to multi_turn_config.oneOf and VertexAIConnectionParams to target_connection_config.anyOf (docs/research/2026-10-19-prisma-airs-openapi/red-team-management-schema-diff.json:197-226 new vs 268-290 old; 170-193 new vs 244-264 old). The identical union-branch additions on the *RedactBase schemas, which were not renamed, ARE digest-bound in REVIEWED_SEMANTIC_CHANGES (lines 39-46, 54-55). So the review gate covers the redacted response variants but not the credential-bearing request/response bases, which are exactly the schemas phase 22 must implement and where the plan's union-order contract lives (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:100-107). I confirmed the old prefix is in fact preserved and the additions are appended, so the recorded decision is substantively correct; the gap is that nothing in the tool or tests enforces or records that.
findings.required_fix: For each component_removed_or_renamed delta, require the successor to satisfy contains(successor, removed_value) for properties/required/type, or bind the successor's exact content to a reviewed digest keyed by (removed_name, successor_name); additionally assert that each successor union list begins with the removed variant's branch list as a prefix. Add regressions in tools/test_red_team_management.py asserting that a successor which drops a property, adds a required field, or reorders an old union prefix raises.

findings.description: The reviewed-digest requirement at 162-165 fires only when path[-1] is a constraint keyword, so it never sees a whole-subtree 'added' delta. Two fail-open paths remain. (a) A newly added property on an existing schema, e.g. ['components','schemas','TargetSchema','properties','new_field'], has a non-constraint leaf and reaches line 206, returning new_behavior_and_alias with no digest review; any nested default/const/pattern/additionalProperties inside that subtree is adopted unreviewed. This already happens: compatibility-decisions.json:307 ('type' const+default 'client_session'), :365/:446/:524 (multi_turn_supported default false) and :899/:912/:935 (additionalProperties true with default {}) are all vendor defaults carried inside opaque added subtrees, and vendor defaults are behaviour-critical under the project's G10 policy. (b) Line 206 matches by prefix, so a future component named e.g. RestConnectionParamsFoo or BasicAuthAuthConfigBar (line 194) or Body_upload_baz (line 196) auto-classifies without anyone reading it, which is precisely the drift-detection contract the plan asserts at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:243-244 ('Unknown changes fail classification'). Phase 25 inherits this classifier.
findings.required_fix: For kind=='added' (and 'removed') deltas whose value is a subtree, require a reviewed digest over the whole identity, or recursively walk the added value and require a digest for any nested default/const/additionalProperties/enum/pattern it introduces. Replace the startswith() prefix matches at 194/196/206 with exact name sets (the current diff has a closed, enumerable set), and add tests asserting that an unknown RestConnectionParams*-prefixed component and an added property carrying a default both raise 'Unclassified'.

findings.description: bindings() merges three pinned audit files into one dict keyed by (source, method, path) with plain assignment at 299, 309 and 311. A key present in more than one audit file is silently overwritten by the last writer, and the coverage assertion at 465 (len(rows)==160 and set(mapping)==set of row keys) still passes because it compares key sets, not provenance. The three sources are currently disjoint by plane, so no collision exists today, but the collision would be invisible rather than fatal, which is inconsistent with the fail-closed posture everywhere else in this tool.
findings.required_fix: Raise on duplicate keys when merging the three audit maps (e.g. assert key not in result before assignment) and add a test that a synthetic overlapping row fails with an explicit duplicate-binding error.

findings.description: impl_contains() matches r'\bfn\s+<method>\s*[(<]' inside a named inherent impl body and does not require pub visibility. A private helper with the same name inside the same impl therefore satisfies a native binding, so the artifact-wide claim 'native_method_exists' (contracts/airs-operations.json:5) is weaker than it reads: it proves an inherent function of that name exists, not that it is part of the public API surface the 160-operation mapping asserts. contracts/native-operations.json is the authoritative public ledger, so this is defence-in-depth rather than an active error.
findings.required_fix: Require the matched function to be preceded by pub (allowing pub(crate) to fail), or cross-check each (class, method) pair against contracts/native-operations.json rustMethods, and add a test that a private inherent fn of the same name does not satisfy a binding.

findings.description: The plan is this phase's primary deliverable, but it carries pervasive typographic defects: missing spaces before numerals throughout (line 13 '0.7.67 to0.86.0', line 14 'Runtime25, Model Security41, Red Team data47 and broker5', line 24 'MSRV1.89', line 32 'js-yaml4.3.2', line 47 '3820 frozen export mappings,448 native methods,23 default bindings,14', line 187 'Phase21', line 252 'every category>=8, total>=42/50 (aim45)'), and a comma splice at lines 50-51 ('...airs-0.2.2-retention.json`, The output is the current inventory'). The same pattern appears in docs/PHASES.md:91-98/133-154 and docs/implementation-plan.md:177-183. None of this changes a decision, but it degrades the readability of the document that phases 22-25 and the drift-detection work will be read against.
findings.required_fix: Proofread docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md, docs/PHASES.md and docs/implementation-plan.md for missing spaces before numerals and the comma splice at lines 50-51, in the same qualified source change.

findings.description: COUNTS is a bare positional list indexed by the audit inventory's spec order (used at 422). The binding between a count and its source is positional only, so a reader cannot tell which number belongs to which spec without cross-referencing inventory.json, and the error message 'Operation count changed: {upstream}' is the only thing that recovers the association. The inventory is hash-pinned so this cannot silently misfire today, but it is the least self-describing constant in a file whose purpose is auditable provenance.
findings.required_fix: Key the expected counts by upstreamPath (a dict) instead of list position, and assert the key set equals the inventory's spec paths.

findings.description: The suite covers build(), disposition(), the retention floor, the tokenizer, metadata verification and the future-phase guard, but nothing exercises the --check stale-artifact path at red_team_management.py:521-523. That comparison is what actually makes the committed contracts/airs-*.json files evidence rather than decoration, and test_future_phase_cannot_pass_on_plan_artifacts invokes --check only for phases 22-25, which abort at the phase guard (line 514) before build() or the comparison runs. A regression that silently stopped writing or comparing one of the five outputs would not be caught by this suite.
findings.required_fix: Add a test that runs the CLI with --check against a temporary tree where one generated artifact has been mutated, asserting nonzero exit and 'Stale contract artifact', and a test asserting all five output paths are produced by build().

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-plan-and-provenance-attempt-04.checks.json records 25 checks, all with resolved `invocation` arrays, exit_code 0 and timeout false, bound to source_sha256 ae5352b1d69acc340c4c9b71352f3c25955d19b7a1dafd4be4a39f046b69860c with source_unchanged true. docs/checks/phase-21.json has the identical header (same checked_at 2026-10-19T13:27:09.020867+00:00) and the same count of 25 exit_code entries. No entry is synthetic, skipped or placeholder.

The 25 recorded commands match tools/check_phase.py:135-175 management_commands(21) exactly in membership and order: the three phase-21 freeze/provenance commands plus the ranged hygiene diff, then the ten `common` commands (two git diff --check with the vendor-YAML exclusion, three verify-contracts modes, red_team_management --check --verify-retention-origin, three unittest suites, private-material receipt), then check-dependencies, test_ci.py, three generator --check tools, verify_native_fixtures --require-test-bindings, red_team_dataplane --check --require-complete, schema-oracle, verify-gateway-specimens, generate_validation, generate_models.

All five attempt-03 findings are closed in current source: CONSTRAINTS (red_team_management.py:29) now spans 30 keywords and the digest gate at 162-165 applies to every delta kind, with test_added_and_changed_constraints_require_exact_review (test file 156-162) covering added enum/pattern and changed default/additionalProperties/items; retained_floor (329-357) emits `current_inventory` plus floorReference and the new test_retention_output_tracks_current_additions (195-205) proves an added export changes the artifact; verify_management_metadata (369-386) reads source.json with a per-field damage test (164-173); rust_code_tokens (211-265) is a single pass that masks comments before strings with test_single_pass_tokenizer_distinguishes_comments_strings_and_code (188-193); the digest procedure is documented in the module docstring (7-11) and in docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:270-278; and the NOTICE obligation is now an explicit phase 22 item at plan lines 205-207.

Provenance chain read end to end: red_team_management.py:35 pins inventory.json 9dd21a24…; build():417 checks the vendored mp-openapi.yaml against the pinned inventory sha256; :444-448 requires json.loads(openapi.json) == the parsed YAML and records normalizedJsonSha256; verify_management_metadata():382 rejects any openapi!=3.1.0, version!=0.86.0 or operation count!=42; contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/source.json:13-15 and contracts/manifest.json:1960-1962 both record sha256 5fbb533b…, gitBlobSha1 9959caca… and 212515 bytes; contracts/airs-active-sources.json:64-73 records the same active spec hash plus normalizedJsonSha256 4d8e6b2f… matching manifest vendorArtifacts:2449.

Vendor ownership is correctly bounded: tools/verify-contracts.py:29 sets VENDOR_ROOTS to contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0 only; :471-478 sweeps the product parent and rejects any file outside a registered version; :479-489 requires exact set equality between manifested and on-disk corpus files; :393-407 requires every vendorArtifact to sit under a registered root, to have a redistributed source inside that root, and to match the source's repository/commit/license and the license record's repository/commit. The --self-test stdout lists 27 rejected tampering cases including unowned-vendor-file, missing-vendor-file, modified-vendor-file, vendor-symlink, vendor-artifact-escape, duplicate-source-id and unowned-vendor-version. The data-plane and Portkey trees are not absorbed, matching the plan's ownership rule at lines 74-76.

Plan claims checked against actual bytes: compatibility-decisions.json:2294-2330 shows TargetConnectionType gains exactly VERTEX_AI and N8N (MS_COPILOT_STUDIO and CUSTOM_TARGET_ADAPTER were already present in 0.7.67); :754-775 shows ResponseMode gains REALTIME; :696-719 shows ProfilingStatus drops INIT/QUEUED and adds NOT_STARTED; :725-743 shows ProfilingStatusFilter is exactly NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED; :2850-2871 shows TargetStatusFilter narrowing from seven values to DRAFT/ACTIVE. Every row of the plan's migration table (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:152-159), including QUEUED having no declared successor and PARTIALLY_COMPLETE being response-only, is corroborated by those enum sets. openapi.json:6605-6609 confirms N8N exists only as an enum member with no dedicated params schema, consistent with the plan adding Vertex fields only.

Delta completeness: compatibility-decisions.json contains 68 deltas and 68 category/decision pairs with no unclassified rows, and 9 'removed' entries (8 three-element component removals plus the Body_upload file.format annotation). test_all_removed_components_have_real_successor (test file 85-92) asserts exactly 8 removals, all categorised component_removed_or_renamed with a successorReference present in the new schema set; COMPONENT_SUCCESSORS (red_team_management.py:63) covers exactly the four *ConnectionParamsBase names times -Input/-Output.

Retention evidence is independent and additive-only: retained_floor (329-357) loads the floor solely from the code-pinned contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json (RETENTION_SHA256 25a77256…), rejects duplicate baselineIds, validates auditedSourceCommit/sdkVersion and the six-entry sourceLedgerSha256 block, then emits the current inventory with floorReference (airs-retained-capabilities.json:23501-23505) rather than a floor copy; verify_retention_origin (360-367) rehashes all six ledgers listed at airs-0.2.2-retention.json:27249-27256. Tests prove removals, emptied rustPaths, a changed default and seed tampering all raise while additions are permitted and never rewrite the seed (test file 214-250).

The planning-metadata exception is enforced byte-exactly: check_phase.py:79-90 require_only_hash_replacements demands each replacement be 64 lowercase hex, appear exactly once as a quoted token in the git baseline bytes, and the substituted result equal the current bytes verbatim; verify_planning_fixture (93-120) then rehashes the actual corpus file and contracts/manifest.json, and verify_planning_gateway_proof (123-132) allows exactly the two allowlisted input hashes and fails if the allowlist is incomplete. crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json:4-12 and contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json:611-614 show the matching provenance chain.

Static-evidence scoping is explicit and fails closed: every operation row carries coverage 'native_method_exists; static_mapping_only; not_live_acceptance' (contracts/airs-operations.json:5); airs-retained-capabilities.json:483 records evidenceLimit deferring old-consumer and round-trip proof to phase 23; active-sources marks management adoptionState pinned_for_phase22_not_runtime_adopted; red_team_management.py:514-515 rejects --require-through-phase 22-25, and test_future_phase_cannot_pass_on_plan_artifacts (test file 252-256) executes the CLI for each of those phases and asserts nonzero exit.

No SDK runtime change: the recorded git diff --exit-code against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e over crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE and the six frozen ledgers exits 0 with the single allowlisted model-regressions exclusion, and the git ls-files --others assertion confirms no untracked SDK file exists. docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:3-12 binds a passing scan (1894 git-visible files, zero selected-value matches) to the same source hash ae5352b1…, and the recorded --check reports receiptFresh true.

Endpoint decision is grounded: the plan's six-constant table (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:170-178) matches real code at crates/scm-sdk/src/constants.rs:631-636, which retains api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com while contracts/airs-operations.json:66-70 records the spec-advertised api.sase.paloaltonetworks.com server, so keeping current defaults under caller destination admission is a conservative, evidenced choice rather than an oversight.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep with Bash disabled: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint ae5352b1d69acc340c4c9b71352f3c25955d19b7a1dafd4be4a39f046b69860c, recompute any file SHA256, run git, or re-execute any of the 25 checks. I verified evidence by reading the recorded invocations, exit codes and stdout, by cross-reading the artifacts those commands assert over, and by confirming the recorded command list matches tools/check_phase.py in content and order.

docs/checks/phase-21.json and docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json are staged-and-modified (AM) in the snapshot git status; I read the working-tree copies and found them consistent with the supplied attempt-04 checks evidence, but I could not diff index against worktree.

The phase-governance chunk artifacts (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, tools/review_phase.py, tools/test_management_phases.py, tools/test_review_phase.py, docs/CI.md, docs/RELEASE.md) are outside this chunk's declared scope. I read tools/check_phase.py only where it owns this chunk's artifacts (the phase-21 command list and the planning-fixture/gateway-specimen gates) and otherwise relied on the passing recorded suites.

Static evidence only, as the artifacts themselves state: native-binding verification proves a named inherent method exists, not request construction, wire acceptance or tenant permissions. Phase 22-25 runtime behaviour, the five response-declaration fixtures, old-consumer source compatibility, MSRV/package qualification and live acceptance are not assessable here and were not judged.

Findings 1 and 2 are reachability arguments from reading disposition() plus greps over the 68 recorded deltas and the research schema diff; I could not execute the function to demonstrate the fail-open paths, so the conclusion that the current output is nevertheless substantively correct rests on that reading.

I read no credential or tenant-registration material and stayed inside the repository; .local/typescript was referenced only as the recorded --baseline argument of verify-contracts.py and was not inspected. I did not verify that the pinned audit inventory's upstream hashes correspond to the real pan.dev commit, since that requires network access the review forbids; the chain is internally consistent and hash-pinned but its upstream anchor is asserted, not re-fetched.
